payload.task_text:
Our company is launching a wellness program and I have been asked to coordinate the cafeteria lunch menu for the upcoming week. There is a corporate nutrition guidelines page available at http://localhost:30206/guidelines.html that outlines the daily nutritional intake targets for a healthy adult, including recommended calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrate amounts per meal, along with notes about common dietary restrictions our employees have reported such as vegetarian and low-sodium preferences.

Please start by visiting that guidelines page and extracting all the nutritional targets and dietary notes listed there. The page has a table with per-meal targets for lunch specifically, and a section listing the top dietary restrictions reported by employees.

Next, search the recipe database for Chinese dishes that would be suitable for a corporate cafeteria lunch. I need you to find at least two main dishes from the meat category, at least two dishes from the vegetable category, and at least one soup or staple dish. For each dish, note the name, category, and any available ingredient or preparation details.

Once you have the recipes, create a Google Sheets spreadsheet called "Wellness_Lunch_Menu" with a sheet named "Weekly_Plan". This sheet should have columns for Day (Monday through Friday), Main_Dish_1, Main_Dish_2, Side_Dish, Soup_Or_Staple, Estimated_Calories, Estimated_Protein_g, Estimated_Fat_g, and Estimated_Carbs_g. Assign the recipes you found across the five days, reusing dishes if needed but trying to vary the menu. Fill in estimated nutritional values per meal based on reasonable estimates for Chinese dishes, keeping them within the guidelines you found on the website. Add a second sheet called "Nutrition_Summary" with columns for Nutrient, Daily_Target, Menu_Average, and Within_Target (Yes or No), with rows for Calories, Protein, Fat, and Carbs.

After the spreadsheet is ready, write a Word document called Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx in the workspace. This document should have a title "Corporate Wellness Lunch Program", a brief introduction explaining the program goals, a section listing the five daily menus with dish names, and a section summarizing how the menu aligns with the nutritional guidelines. Mention any dishes that accommodate dietary restrictions.

Finally, send an email from wellness@company.com to cafeteria-manager@company.com with the subject "Weekly Wellness Lunch Menu - March 2026" that provides an overview of the meal plan, highlights the nutritional targets from the guidelines, and lists all the dishes selected for the week.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, run the four independent read-only sources in one wave and keep their complete page/category responses out of the main context. The recipe categories can exceed the model-output limit, so their owners must be explore sub-agents constrained to read-only source work; they may read the runtime `output_path` but must not write a deliverable or mutate any external system.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 4 explore sub-agents as parallel individual Agent calls:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to read the complete nutrition-guidelines page at `http://localhost:30206/guidelines.html` with read-only browser operations. Return the exact lunch targets for calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrates, every reported dietary restriction/note, and page/table/field controls.
   2. explore 1 (web-domain-researcher 1): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to query exact recipe category `荤菜`. If the response is materialized as an overlong runtime `output_path`, read that file from the task workspace instead of retrying the category call. Select at least two distinct cafeteria-suitable recipe IDs, retrieve only those exact IDs in native parallel, and return `{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], category:"荤菜", category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}`. Do not write a deliverable or modify a recipe.
   3. explore 2 (web-domain-researcher 2): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to query exact recipe category `素菜`. If the response is materialized as an overlong runtime `output_path`, read that file from the task workspace instead of retrying the category call. Select at least two distinct cafeteria-suitable recipe IDs, retrieve only those exact IDs in native parallel, and return `{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], category:"素菜", category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}`. Do not write a deliverable or modify a recipe.
   4. explore 3 (web-domain-researcher 3): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to query exact category `汤`; only when that returned collection has no usable recipe may it query exact category `主食`. Consume any overlong runtime `output_path` from the task workspace without repeating the call, select at least one suitable exact recipe ID, retrieve only that ID, and return `{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], requested_category:"汤", used_category, fallback_reason, category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}`. Do not write a deliverable or modify a recipe.

After Wave 1, the main agent must require at least two meat, two vegetable, and one soup/staple recipe with unique exact IDs, freeze an explicit Monday-Friday menu (reusing only those verified dishes when needed), and derive reasonable meal-level estimates that remain consistent with the source targets. Freeze the task-visible agent-workspace absolute path from the Visible Boundary/current working directory; never assume `/workspace`. From that frozen menu, dispatch the three independent output branches in the same response: (1) coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): own exactly one `Wellness_Lunch_Menu` spreadsheet with `Weekly_Plan` and `Nutrition_Summary` using the task's exact columns/rows; (2) coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): own `<agent_workspace>/Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx` with the exact title, five daily menus, guideline alignment, and supported dietary accommodations; and (3) coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): send exactly one message from `wellness@company.com` to `cafeteria-manager@company.com` with subject `Weekly Wellness Lunch Menu - March 2026`. Read both artifacts once in native-parallel calls, then reconcile dish names, targets, estimates, averages, Within_Target decisions, and email content. Do not dispatch a verification agent.

nodes.text:
You are a read-only web researcher. Your task: visit the corporate nutrition guidelines page at http://localhost:30206/guidelines.html using the playwright browser tools (mcp__playwright_with_chunk__browser_navigate, then mcp__playwright_with_chunk__browser_snapshot to read the accessibility snapshot; use browser_snapshot_search / browser_snapshot_navigate_to_span / browser_snapshot_navigate_to_line as needed to read ALL content, including any tables).

Do NOT write any files, do NOT modify anything, do NOT click buttons or submit forms — strictly read-only.

Extract and return:
1. The exact per-meal (lunch) nutritional targets: calories (kcal), protein (g), fat (g), and carbohydrates (g). Quote the exact numbers and units as shown on the page.
2. Every dietary restriction / dietary note reported by employees (e.g., vegetarian, low-sodium, allergies, etc.) — list each one exactly as written.
3. Any notes about the guideline table or fields (e.g., "per meal" vs "daily").
4. The page title and any other relevant context.

Return the results in a structured format, quoting exact numbers and text from the page. Include the full table contents you find if the table is small; otherwise summarize precisely with exact values.
Read nutrition guidelines page

You are a strictly read-only explore sub-agent. Task: find at least two (2) cafeteria-suitable main dishes from the recipe category "荤菜" (meat dishes).

Steps:
1. Call mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory with category="荤菜" to list all recipes in this category. If the response is materialized as an overlong runtime output_path (e.g., the result says the data was written to a file path), READ that file from the task workspace using terminal commands (cat/head/more on the given absolute path) instead of retrying the category call. The task workspace is /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-playwright-howtocook-nutrition-gsheet-email/workspace — files may be written there or in the given output_path.
2. From the category listing, select at least two DISTINCT recipe IDs that are suitable for a corporate cafeteria lunch (simple, common dishes preferred).
3. Retrieve ONLY those exact selected IDs using mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById in parallel (call them all in one response). Do not fetch any other recipe IDs.
4. If needed, you may use read-only terminal commands to inspect the workspace for any materialized outputs, but you must NOT write any deliverable file or mutate any external system.

Return a JSON object with this exact structure:
{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], category:"荤菜", category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}

Where:
- recipes: array of full recipe details (include ALL ingredients and preparation steps verbatim from the API)
- category_result_count: number of recipes returned for the category
- selected_count: number of recipes you selected
- duplicate_ids: list of any duplicate IDs encountered (empty if none)
- missing_fields: list of any recipe fields that were absent (empty if all present)

Be careful with the tool call parameters — only pass the documented arguments. Do not write deliverables.
Query meat category recipes

You are a strictly read-only explore sub-agent. Task: find at least two (2) cafeteria-suitable dishes from the recipe category "素菜" (vegetable dishes).

Steps:
1. Call mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory with category="素菜" to list all recipes in this category. If the response is materialized as an overlong runtime output_path (e.g., the result says the data was written to a file path), READ that file from the task workspace using terminal commands (cat/head/more on the given absolute path) instead of retrying the category call. The task workspace is /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-playwright-howtocook-nutrition-gsheet-email/workspace — files may be written there or in the given output_path.
2. From the category listing, select at least two DISTINCT recipe IDs that are suitable for a corporate cafeteria lunch (simple, common dishes preferred).
3. Retrieve ONLY those exact selected IDs using mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById in parallel (call them all in one response). Do not fetch any other recipe IDs.
4. If needed, you may use read-only terminal commands to inspect the workspace for any materialized outputs, but you must NOT write any deliverable file or mutate any external system.

Return a JSON object with this exact structure:
{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], category:"素菜", category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}

Where:
- recipes: array of full recipe details (include ALL ingredients and preparation steps verbatim from the API)
- category_result_count: number of recipes returned for the category
- selected_count: number of recipes you selected
- duplicate_ids: list of any duplicate IDs encountered (empty if none)
- missing_fields: list of any recipe fields that were absent (empty if all present)

Be careful with the tool call parameters — only pass the documented arguments. Do not write deliverables.
Query vegetable category recipes

You are a strictly read-only explore sub-agent. Task: find at least one (1) cafeteria-suitable soup or staple dish, preferring category "汤" (soup), with fallback to "主食" (staples) only if the 汤 category has no usable recipe.

Steps:
1. Call mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory with category="汤" to list all recipes in this category. If the response is materialized as an overlong runtime output_path (e.g., the result says the data was written to a file path), READ that file from the task workspace using terminal commands (cat/head/more on the given absolute path) instead of retrying the category call. The task workspace is /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-playwright-howtocook-nutrition-gsheet-email/workspace — files may be written there or in the given output_path.
2. From the category listing, if there is at least one usable recipe (simple, common dish suitable for a cafeteria lunch), select ONE recipe ID. ONLY if the 汤 collection has NO usable recipe, call mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory with category="主食" and select one from there.
3. Retrieve ONLY that exact selected ID using mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById. Do not fetch any other recipe IDs.
4. If needed, you may use read-only terminal commands to inspect the workspace for any materialized outputs, but you must NOT write any deliverable file or mutate any external system.

Return a JSON object with this exact structure:
{recipes:[{recipe_id,name,category,ingredients,preparation}], requested_category:"汤", used_category, fallback_reason, category_result_count, selected_count, duplicate_ids, missing_fields}

Where:
- used_category: "汤" or "主食" (which category the selected recipe actually came from)
- fallback_reason: explanation if you had to fall back to 主食, else null
- category_result_count: number of recipes returned for the category actually used
- recipes: array (usually length 1) of full recipe details including ALL ingredients and preparation steps verbatim from the API
- selected_count: number of recipes selected
- duplicate_ids: list of duplicate IDs encountered (empty if none)
- missing_fields: list of any recipe fields that were absent (empty if all present)

Be careful with the tool call parameters — only pass the documented arguments. Do not write deliverables.
Query soup/staple category recipes

You are an external-workflow operator. Task: create ONE Google Sheets spreadsheet exactly as specified below using the mcp__google_sheet__* tools. Do NOT create any other files or send any emails.

## Spreadsheet specification

1. Call mcp__google_sheet__create_spreadsheet with title "Wellness_Lunch_Menu". Note the returned spreadsheet_id.
2. The new spreadsheet has a default sheet (usually "Sheet1"). Rename that default sheet to "Weekly_Plan" using mcp__google_sheet__rename_sheet (pass spreadsheet, current sheet name, new_name="Weekly_Plan"). If unsure of the default sheet name, call mcp__google_sheet__list_sheets first.
3. Create a second sheet named "Nutrition_Summary" using mcp__google_sheet__create_sheet.
4. Populate the "Weekly_Plan" sheet (header + 5 data rows) using mcp__google_sheet__update_cells with range A1:I6. Use EXACTLY these values (dish names are canonical — copy them character-for-character):

Header: Day | Main_Dish_1 | Main_Dish_2 | Side_Dish | Soup_Or_Staple | Estimated_Calories | Estimated_Protein_g | Estimated_Fat_g | Estimated_Carbs_g

Row1: Monday | 宫保鸡丁 (Kung Pao Chicken) | 凉拌豆腐 (Cold Tofu Salad) | 凉拌油麦菜 (Leaf Lettuce Salad) | 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup) | 585 | 39 | 26 | 58
Row2: Tuesday | 小炒黄牛肉 (Stir-Fried Beef) | 松仁玉米 (Pine Nut Corn) | 凉拌油麦菜 (Leaf Lettuce Salad) | 蛋炒饭 (Egg Fried Rice) | 795 | 37 | 29 | 95
Row3: Wednesday | 宫保鸡丁 (Kung Pao Chicken) | 凉拌豆腐 (Cold Tofu Salad) | 松仁玉米 (Pine Nut Corn) | 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup) | 690 | 41 | 28 | 79
Row4: Thursday | 宫保鸡丁 (Kung Pao Chicken) | 松仁玉米 (Pine Nut Corn) | 凉拌油麦菜 (Leaf Lettuce Salad) | 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup) | 610 | 31 | 25 | 77
Row5: Friday | 小炒黄牛肉 (Stir-Fried Beef) | 凉拌豆腐 (Cold Tofu Salad) | 凉拌油麦菜 (Leaf Lettuce Salad) | 蛋炒饭 (Egg Fried Rice) | 770 | 45 | 30 | 76

Nutritional values should be written as NUMBERS (integers), not text.

5. Populate the "Nutrition_Summary" sheet (header + 4 rows) using mcp__google_sheet__update_cells with range A1:D5. Values:

Header: Nutrient | Daily_Target | Menu_Average | Within_Target
Calories | 650 | 690 | Yes
Protein | 30 | 38.6 | Yes
Fat | 22 | 27.6 | Yes
Carbs | 80 | 77 | Yes

(Daily_Target is the guideline target; Menu_Average is the 5-day average; Within_Target = Yes for all since every average lies within the guideline min-max ranges: Calories 500-800, Protein 20-45, Fat 15-30, Carbs 55-110.)

6. Verify your work: call mcp__google_sheet__get_sheet_data on both sheets (Weekly_Plan range A1:I6, Nutrition_Summary range A1:D5) and confirm the data matches exactly. Fix any mismatch by updating the cells again.

## Return contract
Return a JSON-like summary containing: the spreadsheet_id, the spreadsheet title, the two sheet names, a copy of the final Weekly_Plan data (all 5 rows), a copy of the final Nutrition_Summary data, and confirmation that both reads match what was written.
Create Google Sheets menu

You are an office-report builder. Task: create a Word document at exactly this path:

/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-playwright-howtocook-nutrition-gsheet-email/workspace/Wellness_Menu_Summary.docx

Use the mcp__word__ tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph). Do NOT create a Google spreadsheet and do NOT send emails — only this document.

## Document content (exact structure)

1. Title (Heading 1): "Corporate Wellness Lunch Program"

2. Introduction paragraph(s) (regular paragraphs): Briefly explain program goals — the company is launching a wellness program (March 10-14, 2026, Monday-Friday) and the cafeteria lunch menu should meet the corporate nutrition guidelines established with registered dietitians, featuring balanced Chinese cuisine for a diverse workforce. Mention the program runs March 10-14, 2026.

3. Heading "Five-Day Lunch Menu (March 10-14, 2026)" followed by the five daily menus. Use a subheading or labeled paragraph for each day with the dish names (copy exactly, character-for-character):

- Monday: Main 1 宫保鸡丁 (Kung Pao Chicken); Main 2 凉拌豆腐 (Cold Tofu Salad); Side 凉拌油麦菜 (Leaf Lettuce Salad); Soup 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup)
- Tuesday: Main 1 小炒黄牛肉 (Stir-Fried Beef); Main 2 松仁玉米 (Pine Nut Corn); Side 凉拌油麦菜 (Leaf Lettuce Salad); Staple 蛋炒饭 (Egg Fried Rice)
- Wednesday: Main 1 宫保鸡丁 (Kung Pao Chicken); Main 2 凉拌豆腐 (Cold Tofu Salad); Side 松仁玉米 (Pine Nut Corn); Soup 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup)
- Thursday: Main 1 宫保鸡丁 (Kung Pao Chicken); Main 2 松仁玉米 (Pine Nut Corn); Side 凉拌油麦菜 (Leaf Lettuce Salad); Soup 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup)
- Friday: Main 1 小炒黄牛肉 (Stir-Fried Beef); Main 2 凉拌豆腐 (Cold Tofu Salad); Side 凉拌油麦菜 (Leaf Lettuce Salad); Staple 蛋炒饭 (Egg Fried Rice)

4. Heading "Nutritional Guidelines Alignment" with paragraphs summarizing: the per-meal (lunch) targets from the corporate guidelines (Calories target 650 kcal, range 500-800; Protein target 30 g, range 20-45; Fat target 22 g, range 15-30; Carbohydrates target 80 g, range 55-110), and how the planned menus stay within these ranges. Include the 5-day averages: Calories 690, Protein 38.6 g, Fat 27.6 g, Carbs 77 g — all within the guideline ranges. State that each meal includes a protein-rich main dish (15g+ protein), at least one vegetable dish, and a soup or staple, and that menus vary across the week.

5. Heading "Dietary Accommodations" with paragraphs mentioning how the menu accommodates reported employee restrictions:
- Vegetarian (23%): every day includes a fully vegetarian main option (凉拌豆腐 Cold Tofu Salad or 松仁玉米 Pine Nut Corn), plus vegetarian sides 凉拌油麦菜 (Leaf Lettuce Salad) and 紫菜蛋花汤 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup).
- Low-Sodium (18%): selected dishes use modest soy sauce/salt; dressing-based cold dishes can be prepared with reduced sodium.
- Gluten-Free (12%): most dishes (vegetable dishes, soups, rice-based 蛋炒饭) are naturally gluten-free.
- No Pork (15%): all selected dishes are pork-free (chicken and beef mains), so no pork labeling is required.

6. Optional closing paragraph, e.g., a note that all nutritional values are estimates per single serving and should be confirmed by the cafeteria team.

## Return contract
Return the absolute file path of the created document, confirm it was created, and include a short excerpt (first ~200 chars) of the document text to prove content exists. You may call mcp__word__get_document_text on the file to verify.
Create Word summary document

You are an external-workflow operator. Task: send EXACTLY ONE email using mcp__emails__send_email. Do NOT create spreadsheets, documents, or drafts — only send this one email.

## Email parameters
- from_addr: "wellness@company.com"
- to: "cafeteria-manager@company.com"
- subject (exact): "Weekly Wellness Lunch Menu - March 2026"
- Body: plain text covering (a) an overview of the weekly meal plan, (b) the nutritional targets from the corporate guidelines, and (c) all the dishes selected for the week. Draft the body in English with Chinese dish names as given. Suggested body (you may polish wording but keep all facts and dish names EXACT):

Selected dishes for the week (from our approved Chinese recipe database):

## Return contract
Return the result of the send_email call including any message id or confirmation, and the exact subject/to/from used.
Send wellness menu email
